scenes.text: Ice, water and steam are all the same stuff. Let's follow one ice cube.
Ice is frozen water. Below zero degrees Celsius, water stays solid.
Warm it up to zero degrees and the ice melts into liquid water.
Heat it more. At sea level, water boils at one hundred degrees Celsius.
Boiling turns liquid water into an invisible gas called water vapor.
When vapor cools, it condenses back into tiny droplets. Same water, three states.

steps.heading: Heat makes it *melt*
steps.line: At 0 °C the ice turns to liquid.

steps.heading: Water *boils* at 100 °C
steps.line: That's at sea level. Up a mountain it's lower!

steps.heading: Cool vapor *condenses*
steps.line: The gas turns back into droplets.
